clue.text: Clumsy fish's cry of pain, being swallowed by predator?

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so the cry goes within the predator

parts.note: a seal is a predator that hunts fish
'ow!' is what you cry out when hurt

explanation.surface: A fish yelps in pain as a hungry predator gulps it down.
explanation.walkthrough: The sea owl, also called the lumpsucker, is a squat, slow-swimming fish, which is why the clue calls it clumsy; a seal is apt, being a fish-eater.
explanation.definitionFit: The lumpsucker is an ungainly, round-bodied fish whose other common name is a sea owl.

clue.text: Breton, say, right into certain type of celebrity

indicators.note: the R goes into the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain
an A-list celebrity is one of the most famous kind

explanation.surface: A person from Brittany heads into a certain kind of fame.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into SURE, then A-LIST is added. 'Breton' looks like someone from Brittany, but it is André Breton, founder of the Surrealist movement.
explanation.definitionFit: André Breton wrote the Surrealist Manifesto in 1924 and led that art movement.

clue.text: A new associate setter, in charge of getting extremes of left and right on TV

definitions.text: getting extremes of left and right on TV

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for associate, as in a professional title
the setter of this puzzle signs himself Morph, so the setter's pseudonym is used

explanation.surface: A newly appointed assistant puzzle-maker is put in charge of the TV picture's edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' means this crossword's own compiler, who wrote as Morph in The Independent. An anamorphic picture is squeezed or stretched, so the left and right edges of a wide image fit the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Anamorphic lenses squash a widescreen image horizontally, distorting it towards the sides of the frame.

clue.text: White House frontrunners and independent on the road in case of vote, this lot's hectic campaign trail

indicators.note: the frontrunners of White House are the first letters of its two words

parts.note: St, street, is a road, so something on the road is in the street
lest means in case, for fear that
to opt is to choose, to vote for
our means belonging to us, this lot

explanation.surface: Presidential front-runners and an independent hit the road on a frenzied tour in case the vote turns against them.
explanation.walkthrough: A long charade: WH + I + ST + LEST + OPT + OUR. The political surface makes the whole clue look like a definition, but only the last three words define.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle-stop tour was a politician's rapid round of brief stops, originally at small railway stations.

clue.text: Student has short break in craggy place

indicators.note: the break sits within the craggy place, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff or crag
hol is short for holiday, a break from work

explanation.surface: A student takes a quick holiday somewhere rocky and rugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only links the definition to the wordplay; 'craggy place' is a scar, a word for a crag common in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or someone who studies, especially one holding a scholarship.

clue.text: Miserable about five Euros hoarded

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for miserable wraps the other letters

parts.note: sad means miserable
V is the Roman numeral for five
E is the symbol abbreviation used for euros

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy about having stashed away a few euros.
explanation.walkthrough: SAD goes round V + E.
explanation.definitionFit: Saved and hoarded both mean put money aside rather than spending it.

clue.text: Rigid prescription dashed off on tablet of stone?

definitions.text: dashed off on tablet of stone?
definitions.meaning: read literally: a law written quickly (fast) on something solid (hard), like the commandments on stone tablets

explanation.surface: A strict instruction scribbled hastily on a stone slab.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: 'dashed off' is fast, 'stone' is hard, and a rule carved in stone cannot change.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a fixed regulation allowing no exceptions; literally a law written fast on something firm.

clue.text: Stand over where you might get shuttle

definitions.meaning: to tower over someone in a threatening way
a weaving frame, whose shuttle carries the thread back and forth

explanation.surface: Hovering above the spot where a shuttle might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuttle' suggests a space shuttle or shuttle bus; it is the weaver's shuttle.
explanation.definitionFit: To tower menacingly over something, and the weaving machine through which a shuttle passes the weft thread.

clue.text: Soundtrack for what cavalry did?

parts.note: split the first word as 'sound' plus 'track': a track is a road, and the word sounding like road is what mounted troops did on horseback

explanation.surface: Asking for the music to accompany a cavalry charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundtrack' reads as film music, but split it into 'sound' + 'track': a word that sounds like a track (a road) gives the past tense of ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalry are soldiers on horseback, so what they did was travel mounted.

clue.text: Mind control is phony's game

indicators.note: game here means lame or crooked, as in a game leg, so the letters are twisted round

parts.note: the letters of phony's (the possessive adds an S here) join the fodder

explanation.surface: A fake claims to control minds, and it is all a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' scrambles IS PHONYS, possessive S included, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnosis puts a subject into a trance in which they respond to a hypnotist's suggestions.

clue.text: Fantasist's complaint caused by watching too much Big Brother?

definitions.text: Fantasist's complaint caused by watching too much Big Brother?

parts.words: Fantasist's complaint caused by watching too much Big Brother?
parts.note: Big Brother is a reality television show, so a viewer who binges on it gets too big a dose of so-called real life and loses track of what is true

explanation.surface: Someone who lives in a dream world has been ruined by too much Big Brother.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Brother was a hugely popular British reality TV show. The joke is that an overdose of 'reality' is exactly what would muddle a fantasist.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase plays on an overload, too much of something, of reality television.

clue.text: Scapegoat's inner self-belief

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word scapegoat hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A scapegoat's private self-confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inner' tells you to look inside 'Scapegoat': scap-EGO-at.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is a person's sense of self-importance or self-esteem.

clue.text: Not getting pitch in good condition, English sporting body suffers setback

parts.note: toned describes a body that is fit and firm

indicators.note: a setback sends something backwards, so the sporting body's letters are read the other way

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, the body that runs English football

explanation.surface: An English sports governing body in fine fettle hits a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers setback' turns FA into AF. TONED + E + AF gives the answer. 'pitch' looks like a football pitch but means musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tone-deaf cannot tell musical notes apart by their pitch.

clue.text: A bumpy ride for leftist after revolution

indicators.note: after means the leftist comes behind the word for revolution

parts.note: a rising is an uprising or revolt
Trot is short for Trotskyist, a hard-left activist

explanation.surface: A left-winger has a rough time after the uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests turning round, but here it is a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: In a rising trot the rider bobs up and down in the saddle with the horse's two-beat gait.

clue.text: Queen turns on landlord who's against her?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the Queen comes first
turns means the letters for the Queen are flipped round

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher
a publican is the landlord of a pub

explanation.surface: The Queen rounds on a pub landlord who opposes her.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is turned into RE, then PUBLICAN goes below it. Someone opposed to the monarchy, the 'her' of the clue, favours a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A republican wants a head of state who is elected rather than a monarch.

clue.text: Northern folks' audible mistake

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the folk's name is spoken out loud

parts.note: the Lapps are the people of Lapland in the far north of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A gaffe made by people from the far north that everyone can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: LAPPS said out loud sounds like the answer, 'audible' being the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor error, a brief failure of attention.

clue.text: Spinner's delivery bends out wickedly, taking one in

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the one, holding it inside
together with 'taking', this says one piece goes within another
wickedly means in a wild, unruly way, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A slow bowler's delivery swings out viciously, getting a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' scrambles BENDS OUT, and 'taking ... in' puts I inside that mix. The cricket words (spinner, delivery, bends) are misdirection: the spinner is a spin doctor and the delivery is something he says.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor produces short, quotable remarks for the media, the brief clips used in news reports.

clue.text: For all to see, yes men crawling around Labour leader — indecent!

parts.note: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all audiences

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the first letter of Labour
crawling suggests fawning and squirming, so the letters of yes men are wriggled into a new order
a leader is the first, so take Labour's opening letter

explanation.surface: Sycophants openly fawning over the Labour leader is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawling' scrambles the fodder into NSEEMY, and 'around' puts L inside it. U is the film rating for all audiences; Labour is the British left-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly means improper or not in good taste.

clue.text: Without funds, sets out ways to achieve results from scratch?

definitions.text: ways to achieve results from scratch?

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of sets are rearranged

explanation.surface: Broke, someone lists ways to get results starting from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT plus ESTS ('out' rearranging SETS). The definition puns on 'from scratch': an allergy skin test is done by scratching the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors test for allergies by scratching or pricking the skin and seeing whether it reacts.

clue.text: Farewell or goodbye? These days that is an outdated signifier of class

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the present era of dates
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'
U stood for upper-class usage in the old U and non-U distinction

explanation.surface: Someone muses that saying goodbye in a particular way is now an old-fashioned class marker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U and non-U' was a 1950s British label for upper-class versus middle-class words and habits, now dated.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for parting good wishes, used in English as a formal farewell.

clue.text: Rival operation by potty Geordie conservationists

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot, a potty
a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England, NE
the NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: A rival campaign run by daft conservationists from Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' looks like an adjective meaning crazy but is the noun, a child's chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is someone you compete against, a competitor or adversary.

clue.text: Attack filmed by TV cameras?

definitions.meaning: the start or assault of something, as in the outbreak of an illness
split as two words: being recorded where the filming takes place

explanation.surface: An assault caught on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into two words: being filmed happens 'on set'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an attack or onslaught, and something filmed is happening on a studio set.

clue.text: Get on with filly

definitions.meaning: the posh British pronunciation of girl, and filly is old slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: Get along with a young horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filly' looks like a young horse, but here it is the slang word for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Gel means to combine well with others, and also a 'gel', an upper-class way of saying girl.

clue.text: Sort of examination required if no sound of watch heard?

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing or no

indicators.note: heard means spoken out loud, so the word for the watch's noise is a homophone

parts.note: a watch makes a ticking noise

explanation.surface: Would a check-up be needed if your watch went silent?
explanation.walkthrough: TIC sounds like TICK. The examination is of the ear, which is the organ you hear with.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic means relating to the ear, as in an ear examination by a doctor.

clue.text: Cry over one's potential for growth

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to blub is to cry, British slang

explanation.surface: Weeping over one's ability to develop.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUB is read backwards. A bulb holds a whole plant waiting to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb is a plant's underground store from which a new shoot develops.

clue.text: Artist cast out wretched fellow cut left ear off

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or shape anew, so the word out is rearranged

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of cut, left's L and ear are jumbled

explanation.surface: An artist threw out a wretch who had sliced his ear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges OUT into TOU, and 'off' rearranges CUT + L + EAR into LAUTREC. The ear-cutting brings Van Gogh to mind, but the artist is a different painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was a French painter famous for his posters of Paris nightlife.

clue.text: Queen, perhaps, exposed in it?

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, so the exposed word goes inside the cat

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, one example of a cat
bare means uncovered or exposed

explanation.surface: Is this where a drag queen might be on show?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes the place: a drag queen, perhaps, is exposed to view on a nightclub stage. A queen is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment where performers such as drag queens appear on stage.

clue.text: Muscle can get setter in jam

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Strongman manages to get the crossword compiler into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' and 'in jam' suggest a crossword setter in trouble, but the setter is something that sets jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectin is the natural substance in fruit that makes preserves firm up.
